newsitem.title: USA: S. Calif. homes sales surge in October - report.
newsitem.headline: S. Calif. homes sales surge in October - report.

text.p: Home sales in southern California surged 13 percent in October from the same month last year, with sales continuing at their strongest pace in six years, according to a report released Monday.
A total of 18,505 new and resale houses and condominiums were sold in Los Angeles, Ventura, Orange, Riverside, San Diego and San Bernardino counties in October.
October sales were up 6.8 percent from 17,323 for the month before and up 13.4 percent from 16,320 for October last year, according to DataQuick Information Systems.

So far this year, 162,096 homes were sold in the region, up 17.1 percent from 138,400 for the same period last year. The year-to-date number was the highest since 219,950 were sold during the first 10 months of 1990.

"All the elements are in place," said Donald Cohn, DataQuick's chief executive officer. "The improving economy is creating more jobs, and people are making more money. Home prices are affordable and interest rates are reasonable. The real estate market is not roaring back, but it is recovering at a steady pace."
The year-to-date sales increase was strongest in Orange County, where sale levels were up 23.8 percent.
The lowest rate of increase was in Los Angeles County, where sales were up 11.8 percent year-to-date.

The median price paid for a southern California home was $160,000 last month, down 0.6 percent from $161,000 for the month before and the same as a year ago. The year-to-date median was $160,000, the same as last year.
